title: Reduce Q14 correlated EXISTS overhead with membership caching

steps.step: Inspect the current LDBC full test-data frontier after BENCHPROD-107
Target the Q14 recursive CTE path where per-row correlated EXISTS checks repeatedly scan the same sg delta CTE
Add a narrow membership-cache fast path for single-table EXISTS subqueries of the form local_alias.column = outer_expr
Keep all unsupported EXISTS shapes on the existing bound-subquery fallback path
Add regression coverage for aliased NOT EXISTS membership filtering
Run Rust regressions, release PgWire integration tests, release build, and a non-isolation full test-data LDBC smoke

result.current_frontier: The correlated EXISTS membership cache is covered and does not break PgWire or SQL regressions, but full test-data non-isolation LDBC still stalls in the Q14 performance frontier.

remaining_blockers: Full test-data non-isolation LDBC still times out after 4 operations when Q14 is enabled.
This BENCHPROD-108 smoke is gap evidence, not a full official/native LDBC benchmark pass.
Q14 likely needs deeper recursive-CTE pruning, join ordering, indexed edge expansion, or a targeted Q14 profiler beyond the simple membership cache.
The configured LDBC PostgreSQL implementation still logs missing update-query files, so update coverage is not proven.
Native memtier remains blocked by missing real memtier_benchmark tooling.
next_task: BENCHPROD-109 candidate: build a targeted Q14 profiler/harness to measure recursive search_graph row growth and separate recursive expansion time from downstream paths/edges/weights aggregation.
